source_text:
3.8 Τοῦ αὐτοῦ· πρὸς τὸ μὴ
ἐκτιτρώσκειν ἔμβρυον Τὴν ἐχενηΐδα τὸν ἰχθὺν λαμβάνοντες ναῦται ταριχεύουσιν
εἴς τε τὸ μὴ ἐξαμβλίσκειν καὶ εἰς σύλληψιν ὡς ἐρρωμενεστέρῳ φαρμάκῳ χρώμενοι. Ἐξ ἧς λειουμένης τὸ ζῷον ἐγχυματιζόμενον τὸ ἐν τῇ γαστρὶ σῶον διατηρεῖ. Εἰ δὲ καὶ
ζῶσαν προσενέγκοι τις τῇ νηδύϊ τῆς ἱππάδος, ὅτε ταύτῃ ὁ ἵππος συνέρχεται, καὶ τότε
καὶ εἰς τὸ λοιπὸν συλλήψεται καὶ οὐδέποτε πείσεται τὸν προειρημένον ὄλισθον.
pass_a_gloss: 3.8 Of-the-same: toward the not to-miscarry an-embryo. The echeneis the fish taking sailors pickle both into the not to-abort and into conception as with-a-stronger drug using. From which being-pounded the animal being-drenched the in-the-belly sound keeps. If but also a-living-one someone should-apply to-the-belly of-the-mare, when with-this the stallion comes-together, both then and into the remaining she-will-conceive and never will-suffer the aforesaid slip.
pass_b_english: Of the same: toward not miscarrying an embryo. Sailors take the echeneis, the fish, and pickle it, using it as a stronger drug both for not aborting and for conception. From it, being pounded, the animal that is drenched keeps what is in the belly sound.
And if someone should also apply it living to the belly of the mare when the stallion comes together with her, she will conceive both then and for the rest, and will never suffer the aforesaid slip.

choices.why: Both verbs are miscarriage of the embryo. Not 'destroy' or 'extend'.
Sailors salt-preserve the remora as a drug. Not mere storage.
νηδύς is the belly/womb. ἱππάς is the mare. Not a naiad or a generic horse.
Same Cesti drench as 3.5–3.7. Not mix or rub.
ὄλισθος is the slip of the embryo (miscarriage). πείσεται is suffer, not be persuaded.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
